messages.subject: 14th International Conference on Multilevel Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Sorry for any cross-posting. Note that the conference this year is in March rather than in April.  Also, this year's multilevel conference immediately precedes the Meeting of the SEM Working Group:  https://www.utwente.nl/en/et/dpm/chair/pmr/semg/

SAVE THE DATE and Call for Abstracts: The International Conference on Multilevel Analysis

The 14th International Multilevel Conference will be held on March 12-13, 2024.

The conference will be about all aspects of statistical multilevel analysis: innovative applications, theory, software, and methodology. The conference will be in an informal style, with much room for discussion. It will be held in the city centre of Utrecht, within a quarter hour walk or a five-minute bus ride from the Central railway station.

Keynote speakers include dr. Mirjam Moerbeek on sample size calculations and professor Dan McNeish on measurement in intensive longitudinal data. A first pre-conference workshop on extracting personalised latent dynamics using multilevel HMMs is taught by dr. Emmeke Aarts and a second pre-conference workshop on projection predictive variable selection is taught by Dr. Andrew Johnson

Abstract submission

Deadlines for submitting an abstract: If you submit before the 1st of November (2023), you will be notified on the 15th of November if your abstract is accepted. If you submit before the 7th of January (2024), you will be notified on the 21st of January if your abstract is accepted.

This edition of the conference will also have the option for researchers working with empirical data to submit posters with questions about their analyses or sampling design. During the conference you will have the opportunity to receive feedback on your (ongoing) research.

Young Researcher Award

The abstracts of four PhD students will be selected and these PhD students will be invited to present their work in a special symposium. The best presentation will be awarded during the closing ceremony with the 'Best PhD Multilevel Presentation Award' and their conference fee will be reimbursed.

Pre-conference workshops

There will be two pre-conference workshop(s) on March 11th. One of these is a workshop on extracting personalised latent dynamics using multilevel HMMs is taught by dr. Emmeke Aarts. A hands-on workshop on projection predictive variable selection for multilevel models using the R-package projpred will be taught by Dr. Andrew Johnson. Andrew will introduce the motivations behind and benefits of projection predictive selection, with an emphasis on practical application and real-world problems. Andrew is a postdoc with Aki Vehtari's group at Aalto University (Helsinki), who are the primary developers and maintainers of the projpred package. Andrew is also part of the development team for Stan, the increasingly popular program for Bayesian analysis.

The conference website with further information on abstract submission can be found at http://multilevel.fss.uu.nl/ <https://eur04.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fmultilevel.fss.uu.nl%2F&data=05%...%40uva.nl%7C8e6872fa97d64f76abc608dbd6d33bcd%7Ca0f1cacd618c4403b94576fb3d6874e5%7C0%7C0%7C638339974972137719%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=5W18vgiltbYZKLvJxYngFpHD0juv2OOeCchmaaDX4g4%3D&reserved=0>

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

To continue with this thread, I've noticed the blavCompare no longer yields values for the Bayes factor in examples when it had previously. Picking up on the example Pedro started in this thread and revised code sent by Mauricio, I ran the following code

library(lavaan)
library(blavaan)

hsm1 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit1 <- bcfa(hsm1, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, meanstructure=T)
hsm2 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6 + x7
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit2 <- bcfa(hsm2, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, meanstructure=T)
blavCompare(fit1, fit2)

This returns values for most of the results (WAIC and LOO), but returns NA for the approximation to the log-Bayes factor. Can you advise?

Thanks blavaan folks for the terrific package, and attentiveness to user issues,
Roy

messages.body_plain:
Hi Roy

I think with the updates in blavaan the marginal LL is not calcuates automatically anymore. Not sure if Ed plans to add it again

But for now, we could do a few edits and calculate the BF with the bridgesampling package. By telling blavaan to save some of the underlying parameters

I have doubt about making a tutorial about this, because I persoanlly dont like the BF much. But I understand people like it. Also, we could switch the blavaan recommendation from the approximate log-BF to the bridgesampling method

library(blavaan)
library(lavaan)
library(bridgesampling)

origpars <- c("Lambda_y_free", "B_free", "Theta_sd_free", "Theta_r_free",
              "Psi_sd_free", "Psi_r_mat", "Psi_r_free", "Nu_free",
              "Alpha_free", "Tau_ufree",
              "z_aug",
              "Lambda_y_free_c","B_free_c", "Theta_sd_free_c",
              "Theta_r_free_c",
              "Psi_sd_free_c", "Psi_r_mat_c", "Psi_r_free_c", "Nu_free_c",
              "Alpha_free_c")

hsm1 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit1 <- bcfa(hsm1, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,

             meanstructure=T,
             mcmcextra = list(monitor = origpars))

hsm2 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6 + x7
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit2 <- bcfa(hsm2, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,

             meanstructure=T,
             mcmcextra = list(monitor = origpars))

blavCompare(fit1, fit2)

bs1 <- bridge_sampler(fit1@external$mcmcout)
bs2 <- bridge_sampler(fit2@external$mcmcout)

bf(bs1, bs2)

messages.subject_clean: Fitting growth models in blavaan using the formula function
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am interested in knowing if the formula function in R can be used with blavaan.  Specifically,  I have been successfully able to use the formula function in R to fit 4 simple Stan glm models

```
fits <- list()

fits[[1]] <- stan_glm(PV1READ ~ 1, data = PISAdata, seed = 832762) # This is the baseline model
fits[[2]] <- update(fits[[1]], formula = PV1READ ~ Female + ESCS + HOMEPOS + ICTRES) # model 1 variables
fits[[3]] <- update(fits[[1]], formula = PV1READ ~ JOYREAD + PISADIFF + SCREADDIFF + SCREADCOMP) # model 2 variables
fits[[4]] <- update(fits[[1]], formula = PV1READ ~ METASUM + GFOFAIL + MASTGOAL + SWBP + WORKMAST + ADAPTIVITY + COMPETE) # model 3 variables
fits[[5]] <- update(fits[[1]], formula = PV1READ ~ PERFEED + TEACHINT + BELONG) # model 3 variables
```
This is followed by further code for what I needed to do.  What I would like to do is use this formula and update functionality for fitting different growth models.  Is that possible?

Thanks

Hi David,

There is not currently an update() method for blavaan. If you try to use it, I believe R will try to use update() from lavaan and throw some errors.

For rstanarm, I am not sure that update() gives you any computational speedups. I think it just saves typing because you only need to specify a new formula without sending in the data and other arguments. I think that an approach like the following would also work for blavaan:

modelargs <- list(formula = "PV1READ ~ 1", data = PISAdata, seed = 832762)
fits[[1]] <- do.call("stan_glm", modelargs)

modelargs$formula <- "PV1READ ~ Female + ESCS + HOMEPOS + ICTRES"
fits[[2]] <- do.call("stan_glm", modelargs)

modelargs$formula <- "PV1READ ~ JOYREAD + PISADIFF + SCREADDIFF + SCREADCOMP"
fits[[3]] <- do.call("stan_glm", modelargs)

and so on.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Issue with blavCompare
messages.body_plain:
Roy, Mauricio,

I did not intend to turn off marginal log-likelihood completely, and I believe the CRAN version of blavaan has a bug that makes these NA. The issue should be fixed on github, and it should make its way to CRAN in the coming weeks.

Marginal log-likelihood is turned off for some models, including

- those where model covariance matrices are neither block diagonal nor unrestricted

- models with ordinal variables

- two-level models

In these cases, it can be tough to evaluate the prior and/or likelihood.

The marginal likelihoods that are supplied use a Laplace approximation, and I am not convinced that the approximation works well. More work could be done to evaluate these metrics as applied to SEM.

Ed

I agree that the concept and interpretation of Bayes factors is nice, and I am not as worried about sensitivity to priors as some others are. My main concerns are computational: the Bayes factor is difficult to compute in general, and there are many ways to make a mistake without realizing it. We described some SEM-specific computational difficulties in the "opaque prior distributions" paper:

https://doi.org/10.5964/meth.11167

Best,
Ed

messages.subject: Re: How to get standardized posterior estimates in output summary?
messages.subject_clean: How to get standardized posterior estimates in output summary?
messages.body_plain:
with the same argument as in lavaan in the summary function

library(blavaan)
library(lavaan)

# The Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit, standardized=T)
